messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: SDK client 3.7.0 canary exhibiting streaming handshake failures in prod (api-gateway).
alice.nguyen: Heads up — seeing 502/stream aborts from canary hosts starting ~2234567880. small spike but consistent for long-lived streams.
alice.nguyen: Logs show 'handshake mismatch: client proto=3.7.0 server=3.6.x' for affected sessions.
alice.nguyen: I reproduced locally: client 3.7.0 -> server 3.6.5 fails handshake.
bob.smith: Confirmed. We bumped the frame header enum in 3.7.0 and didn't maintain backward compatibility for streaming handshakes. My bad.
bob.smith: This will break clients that open persistent streams and don't fallback.
dave.m: Canary group = 2 hosts in us-west-2, traffic split 5% canary / 95% stable. Impacting ~0.4% of streaming sessions currently.
carol_pm: Which tenants hit the canary hosts? any paying customers affected?
support-bot: Top affected tenants: acme-inc (8 sessions), betaworks (3 sessions), internal-infra (5 sessions).
alice.nguyen: User-visible: mid-session stream abort (502) and clients see reconnect attempts. No data loss reported yet.
bob.smith: Immediate mitigation options: flip feature flag to disable new handshake behavior for canary OR rollback/republish SDK. FF is faster.
alice.nguyen: I'll flip the canary FF now, targetting canary hosts only.
deploy-bot: /ff set sdk_streaming_v3_canary false --env=canary --by=alice.nguyen
deploy-bot: feature flag updated: sdk_streaming_v3_canary=false
alice.nguyen: Watching metrics — error rate on canary hosts falling within 90s :eyes:
dave.m: Nice. Next: do we roll back the published 3.7.0 artifact or cut a 3.7.1 patch?
bob.smith: I'll prepare a minimal handshake encoding fix and aim for 3.7.1. Patch ETA ~2h if CI is green. Short term FF kill is safest.
carol_pm: Product ok with FF kill. Support, prepare customer comms for acme-inc + betaworks.
support-bot: Draft message ready: "We detected an issue with SDK 3.7.0 streaming handshake for some canary clients. We disabled the canary behavior and impacted sessions are recovering. A patch release is in progress; we'll follow up with an ETA." Approve to send?
carol_pm: Approve. Send to account teams and ticket owners.
dave.m: I'll open a postmortem stub. Root cause: incompatible SDK client header enum. Mitigation: FF kill for canary + patch release.
incident-bot: Incident severity adjusted: S2 (reduced after mitigation). Timeline entry created.
alice.nguyen: On-call handoff: I'm handing to @eve.sre for overnight monitoring. Things to watch: stream-abort rate, alert flapping, regressions if we toggle flag back.
dave.m: @eve.sre — action checklist copied to you. Silence alert rule #streaming-handshake for 30m while we validate.

alice.nguyen: Logs / quick queries for handoff:

```
# find handshake mismatches
kubectl logs -l app=api-gateway -n prod | grep "handshake mismatch"
```

alice.nguyen: Also saved a grep + sample payloads to /var/tmp/stream-handshake-samples.tar.gz

eve.sre: taking over on-call. I'll monitor error rate for the next 4h and watch for FF side effects.
bob.smith: I'll post an ETA and PR link once 3.7.1 is green, then coordinate staged publish. Plan: smoke on staging -> publish to registry -> don't auto-bump clients.
carol_pm: Request for post-incident actions: 1) add a compatibility unit test for streaming handshake between client versions, 2) add canary rollback playbook snippets + who flips FF, 3) communicate root cause to infra teams.
dave.m: Agree. I'll add those to runbook and assign owners.
alice.nguyen: Thanks all. I'll update thread if anything changes.
carol_pm: Thanks — keep incident channel updated. :thumbsup:
